title: Simplified Tonkotsu-Style Ramen
subtitle: Rich pork and miso broth with soft-boiled eggs
excerpt: A proper tonkotsu takes 12 hours, but this simplified version builds a deeply flavoured broth in about an hour using pork shoulder and plenty of aromatics. The miso adds the richness that the short cooking time cannot fully develop. It is very good indeed.
sourceNotes: Tonkotsu ramen originated in Kurume, Fukuoka prefecture, in the 1940s. The bone-heavy, opaque white broth became a defining style of southern Japanese ramen and is now famous worldwide.

recipe.freezeNotes: The broth (without noodles) freezes well for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the broth up to 2 days ahead. Reheat gently and cook the noodles fresh.

content.text: For the soft-boiled eggs, bring water to the boil, lower in the eggs and cook for exactly 6 minutes 30 seconds, then transfer to ice water. Peel and halve just before serving.
Put the pork shoulder, garlic and ginger in a large pot. Pour over the chicken stock and bring to the boil. Skim off any grey foam that rises to the surface.
Reduce to a steady simmer and cook for 60 minutes until the pork is very tender. Lift the pork out and shred into chunks using two forks.
Strain the broth through a sieve back into the pot. Whisk in the miso, dark soy and sesame oil. Taste and adjust seasoning. Keep at a gentle simmer.
Blanch the pak choi in the broth for 2 minutes. Remove and set aside. Cook the noodles according to the packet, drain and divide between four deep bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over the noodles. Top each bowl with shredded pork, pak choi, a halved soft-boiled egg and spring onions.

items.cause: Not enough reduction or too much stock.
items.fix: Boil the broth uncovered for 15 minutes to reduce.

items.symptom: Pork is still tough after an hour
items.cause: Some shoulder pieces need longer to break down.
items.fix: Cook for 20 more minutes and check again.
